target.title: fix(scripts): preserve surrogate pairs when truncating LLM text in bench dump
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`scripts/repro/tool-surface-live-bench.ts` uses `String.prototype.slice(0, N)` at three sites to truncate LLM output text for benchmark trail/log output. `slice` operates on UTF-16 code units, so when a surrogate pair (emoji, CJK character) straddles the cut boundary at position 299-300 or 399-400, the result contains an unpaired high surrogate — invalid Unicode that downstream consumers may reject.

## Why This Change Was Made

Replace with `truncateUtf16Safe` from `@openclaw/normalization-core/utf16-slice`, the same helper already used across the codebase for safe UTF-16 boundary truncation. Sibling UTF-16 PRs (#104054, #107664, #109561, #109498, #109839) all use the same helper. The 300- and 400-code-unit limits and all non-truncated output remain unchanged.

Collision check: no open same-file or same-problem PR was found.

## User Impact

Benchmark trail and result dump output no longer produces invalid Unicode. No production impact — this file is a `scripts/repro/` bench tool.

## Evidence

### Format and diff check

```
$ git diff --check origin/main..HEAD && echo ok
ok
```

### Focused test suite

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs test/scripts/tool-surface-live-bench.test.ts
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  8 passed (8)
```

### Real behavior proof — bench run against mock OAI Responses endpoint

A loopback mock HTTP server on 127.0.0.1:19876 returns OAI Responses API SSE with boundary-straddling text (🐱 at UTF-16 positions [299,300] and [399,400]). The bench is invoked with `BENCH_DUMP=1` and `--providers=openai --surfaces=direct --tasks=top-plot`. This exercises the exact production code path through the Agent → model fetch → stream processing → trail dump pipeline.

**Before fix** (raw `.slice(0, N)`) — the ASSISTANT trail text ends with U+FFFD (terminal rendering of unpaired surrogate), and the result JSON `finalText` field contains a trailing `\ud83d` (unpaired high surrogate):

```
===== DUMP openai/direct/top-plot ok=false =====
ASSISTANT text: xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx...xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx�
===== END DUMP =====
... "finalText": "...xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx🐱yyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyy\ud83d"
```

**After fix** (`truncateUtf16Safe`) — the ASSISTANT trail text is clean (299 chars, surrogate pair dropped at boundary), and `finalText` has no trailing surrogate (399 chars, first 🐱 preserved intact, second 🐱 at 399-400 dropped correctly):

```
===== DUMP openai/direct/top-plot ok=false =====
ASSISTANT text: xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx...xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx
===== END DUMP =====
... "finalText": "...xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx🐱yyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyy"
```

Site-by-site analysis at this exact head (6a23f108ec5c):
- **site1** (ASSISTANT text, 300-unit boundary): `truncateUtf16Safe` returns 299 code units, no trailing surrogate. Raw `.slice(0,300)` retains U+D83D at position 299.
- **site2** (TOOLRESULT, 400-unit boundary): same helper, same boundary logic; covered by the 8 unit tests validating the 400-unit path.
- **site3** (finalText, 400-unit boundary): `truncateUtf16Safe` returns 399 code units with the first 🐱 intact, no trailing surrogate. Raw `.slice(0,400)` retains U+D83D at position 399.

### Not tested

- Live multi-provider LLM bench against real OpenAI/Anthropic/Google endpoints (requires production API keys)
- TOOLRESULT truncation site with boundary-straddling tool output (the identically-named call path uses `truncateUtf16Safe` with the same limit and is covered by the unit tests)
